title: Serialization and Data Persistence Basics
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of serialization and data persistence basics using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates serialization and data persistence basics.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Serialization and Data Persistence Basics** as part of **Exceptions, Files, and Input/Output**. Serialization converts values to a defined external format; Kotlin serialization needs its plugin and format library, and untrusted input still requires validation. Use the subtopics—Serialization Concepts, Structured Data and File Formats, Data Validation on Read—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

items.title: Serialization Concepts
items.text: Serialization Concepts crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

items.title: Structured Data and File Formats
items.text: Structured Data and File Formats is one part of serialization and data persistence basics. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Data Validation on Read
items.text: Data Validation on Read defines a trust boundary. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, keep secrets server-side, check authorization where the protected operation occurs, and test both allowed and rejected cases.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Parsing external JSON makes its values trustworthy without validation.
